featured_reviews.name: vishal kudtarkar
featured_reviews.review_text:
First Car Experience Ruined – False Promises & Huge Financial Loss

This was my first car purchase, and unfortunately, it turned into one of the worst buying experiences of my life.

I saw the car in the first week of January 2025. Since I was a first-time buyer and not fully aware of technical details, I trusted the dealer. I paid a token amount after they promised delivery within a couple of weeks and assured me that all issues like minor dents, polishing, AC work, clutch work, etc. would be fully resolved before delivery.

On the delivery day, the car was nowhere near ready. Shockingly, no work had been done at all even after taking the token. Only when I arrived in the morning did they start working on the car. I had to wait the entire day and finally got delivery at 8:30 PM, which is unacceptable.

Within one week, the engine check light came on. The car started overheating and had issues with the crankshaft sensor and timing belt. I contacted them immediately. They asked me to give the car for “2 days,” which turned into 10–12 days. I had to keep calling repeatedly with no clear response.

Even after that, the car still had issues. They assured me that since the ownership transfer was not done yet, I could use the car for 15 days and they would replace it if problems continued. After those 15 days, the situation became worse—the car barely gave 5 kmpl, despite being promised 13–15 kmpl.

When checked at another workshop, I was informed the engine had major back compression issues, with repair estimates of ₹1.3–1.5 lakh. After this, the dealer became unreachable, saying the office was closed or that they were out of town—for 1–2 months.

Left with no choice, I sold the car and suffered a loss of nearly 45% of the purchase amount within just a few months.

After this entire experience, I did some research on my own and noticed that the dealer has a workshop located on the opposite side of the road from the showroom. From what I could observe and understand, many cars appear to be worked on there—repaired, repainted, and fixed for defects—before being sold.

This explains why their pricing is slightly lower compared to other dealers. However, these cars are presented as being in excellent or “ready” condition, while in reality they seem to be heavily worked-on vehicles rather than genuinely problem-free ones.

As a customer, this lack of transparency is extremely concerning, especially for first-time buyers who trust the dealer’s word.

This was my first and last car from this dealership. I’m sharing this review so others don’t go through the same stress, time loss, and financial damage.

Avoid Asian Motors Bhayandar at all costs.
Bought Hero Xtreme 125R BS6 Phase 2 in November 2025. 7 issues in 6 months on a brand new motorcycle:
Bike jerking at 3500-4500 RPM since day one — ignored for 6 months across multiple services until I forcefully escalated
Promised accessories withheld at delivery — rear hugger, bike cover delayed across 3-4 visits, rusted nuts used on number plate
Clutch assembly nuts coming loose every 200-300km on a 1951km motorcycle — critical safety defect
Bluetooth connectivity — gave completely wrong technical explanation showing zero product knowledge
ABS sensor, cruise control and check engine light all non-functional at delivery — needed external engineer to diagnose
Extremely hard gearbox — only fixed after excessive escalation
Bike geometry dangerously messed up after service — loose steering head bearing causing instability at all speeds, potential tank slapper risk
Salesperson denied PDI at delivery. Service center consistently dismissive and incompetent.
Formally escalating to Hero MotoCorp customer care. Consumer court is next step if unresolved.
I have documented evidence of all issues mentioned above

featured_reviews.name: Hardik Jaitly
featured_reviews.review_text:
From car breaking down on its way to home to numerous concern following up. Took a loss of over 1 lakh in a couple of months for my own mistake of trusting someone and not actually getting a vehicle checked.
Post sales service was a nightmare. Everytime my car was to be picked up ( i decided to sell it back to them as they had a customer available ) or anything as such, there was a personal problem following up to weeks of call ignorance.
When they finally came to buy my car again which was sold by them, my car decided to turn off as battery was not charged. Later they took the money back and left the car. I really wished I did it when the car got me stranded on a highway again.
I did suffer because of my own mistake. Took a loss of over approximately 1 lakh 20 thousand for not doing my checks well.
Purchased the car for 130k approx, spent another 40-50k ( car had rusting in chassis, all damaged parts in engine, etc) and sold the car for 65,000.
When we went to buy the car, same car was a hot selling car and had good engine work done hence there was no scope of negotiation and when I went to sell it back, engine work did not matter just the bodyline mattered.
You definitely meet two different people in same person. When you go to buy, its the best experience. When you go back with issues witin first day or two - “the car was good when it was with us. Now we cant do anything.”
PS - after my car turning off on the same day of delivery and me towing the car back home, they definitely helped me out by sending a mechanic home who swapped the battrey with a different car and also changed the alternater belt which all failed in less than 24 hrs.

Last but not the least, when I was making the payment my friend who had dealt with them in past told me - dont buy from them as he had already done that mistake but I did not listen. So yes, its not them but its my mistake  overall.

Currently, I purchased a car from Spinny and enjoying every bit of it.

featured_reviews.name: Kabir Kabir
featured_reviews.review_text:
I went to Janta Garage, Mira Road to fix a noise coming from the front left wheel area of my Honda WRV. I was told the issue would be resolved after servicing.

I ended up spending more than ₹10,000, but after the service, the same noise was still there. When I went back and questioned them, I was told that “another part needs to be replaced” and they did not have that part earlier.

This raises a serious question:

If the actual faulty part was not replaced, WHY did I pay ₹10k in the first place?

The original cost should have been around ₹6,000, but it suddenly went up to ₹10,000+ without proper explanation. It honestly felt like a complete scam.

Important Warning to Customers:
•	Always ask for the old spare parts to be returned
•	Don’t trust blindly if you are not standing there while work is being done
•	Get a clear written estimate before approving any work

In my case, I trusted them and ended up wasting money with no solution. This garage is NOT transparent, and I would not recommend Janta Garage, Mira Road to anyone looking for honest or reliable car repair.

It’s better to find a trustworthy mechanic who explains the issue clearly and doesn’t overcharge.
